description: A four-panel composite (a-d) characterising the hot rolled & quenched (HRQ) specimen of a high (~5 wt.%) Al low-density medium-Mn steel; it mixes optical microscopy, SEM, EDS and EBSD. (a) Optical micrograph with a 100 µm scale bar showing light-coloured, elongated δ-ferrite islands stretched along the rolling direction inside a darker matrix; the inset is a differential interference contrast (DIC) image labelling δ and α/γ. (b) SEM micrograph, 10 µm scale bar, again labelled δ and α/γ, the α/γ regions showing lenticular, internally structured relief consistent with martensite. (c) EDS spectrum, x-axis 0.00-9.00 keV, y-axis 'Lsec: 20.0' (no numeric count scale), with labelled C, Al, Si, Mn and two Fe peaks, plus an inset table of composition; a second supplied image in the group is a magnified duplicate of this panel. (d) EBSD phase map superimposed on the IQ map, RD/ND arrows at lower left, 100 µm scale bar, legend BCC (red) and FCC (green). Together the panels argue that hot rolling plus water quenching eliminates the dendritic structure, aligns δ-ferrite and α/γ along RD, and transforms part of the austenite to martensite, with Mn enriched in austenite/martensite and Al in δ-ferrite.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph of the HRQ specimen, 100 µm scale bar, showing light-coloured elongated δ-ferrite islands (a few tens of µm long) oriented along the rolling direction in a darker α/γ matrix. The inset is a DIC image in which the light phase is labelled δ and the darker phase α/γ.

SEM micrograph, 10 µm scale bar, labelled δ in the large featureless grey areas and α/γ in the structured grains, which display fine lenticular/needle relief and internal parallel striations typical of martensite laths.

EDS spectrum, x-axis 0.00-9.00 keV with 1 keV major ticks, detector annotation 'Det Octane Elect Plus', y-axis marked 'Lsec: 20.0'. Labelled peaks: C (~0.28 keV), a low-energy Fe/Mn pair, Al (~1.5 keV), Si (~1.7 keV), Mn (~5.9 keV), and two Fe peaks (~6.4 and 7.06 keV). The inset table gives Al (wt%) = 5.61±0.11 in δ-Ferrite and 4.75±0.11 in Austenite/Martensite; Mn (wt%) = 7.02±0.25 in δ-Ferrite and 8.36±0.16 in Austenite/Martensite.

EBSD phase map superimposed on the image-quality (IQ) map, with RD/ND orientation arrows at lower left and a 100 µm scale bar; legend BCC = red, FCC = green. Green FCC islands of elongated lens/ellipse shape are distributed in a red BCC matrix that also retains a faint internal structure.

The second supplied image is a magnified reproduction of panel (c) only, in which the EDS peak labels and the composition table (Al and Mn in wt.% for δ-Ferrite and Austenite/Martensite) become fully legible.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an optical micrograph with a 100 µm scale bar showing light-coloured elongated δ-ferrite islands elongated along the rolling direction within a darker matrix.
The DIC inset inside panel (a) labels the light phase as δ and the darker phase as α/γ.
Panel (b) is an SEM micrograph with a 10 µm scale bar in which the α/γ grains show fine lenticular, internally striated relief while the δ regions appear featureless grey.
Panel (d) is an EBSD phase map overlaid on the IQ map with a 100 µm scale bar; the legend assigns BCC to red and FCC to green, and RD/ND arrows are drawn at the lower left.
In panel (d) the green FCC phase forms elongated lens-shaped islands embedded in the red BCC matrix.
The inset table of panel (c) prints Al (wt%) = 5.61±0.11 for δ-Ferrite and 4.75±0.11 for Austenite/Martensite, and Mn (wt%) = 7.02±0.25 for δ-Ferrite and 8.36±0.16 for Austenite/Martensite.

The EDS spectrum in panel (c) spans 0.00-9.00 keV and carries labelled C, Al, Si, Mn and two Fe peaks, with the detector noted as 'Det Octane Elect Plus' and the vertical axis marked 'Lsec: 20.0' rather than a numeric count scale.

The EDS analysis of the HRQ sample gives Mn and Al concentrations in the δ ferrite phase of 7.02±0.25 wt.% and 5.61±0.11 wt.%, respectively, while in the austenite/martensite phase Mn and Al are 8.36±0.16 wt.% and 4.75±0.11 wt.%, showing Mn enrichment in austenite/martensite and Al enrichment in δ ferrite.
Dendritic structures are reported to be completely eliminated in the HRQ sample due to soaking at higher temperature, and grains of both phases are elongated in the rolling direction.

Water quenching from the rolling finish temperature (~800 °C) is said to transform part of the austenite into lenticular martensite, as shown in Fig. 3b and confirmed by the DIC inset of Fig. 3a and the EBSD phase map in Fig. 3d.

A martensite start temperature of ~350 °C was calculated from the empirical equation given in the cited references, supporting the austenite-to-martensite transformation on water quenching; the remaining austenite is termed untransformed austenite.

The caption states the specimen is the hot rolled & quenched (HRQ) material and identifies the phases as ά-martensite, γ-austenite and δ-delta ferrite, with RD = rolling direction and ND = normal direction.
The caption describes panel (a) as an optical microscopic image with a DIC inset, panel (b) as an SEM image, panel (c) as EDS analysis and panel (d) as an EBSD phase map superimposed on an IQ map.
The second supplied image in this group is a magnified crop of panel (c) and contains no additional panels or data.

unreadable_items: panel (c): the vertical scale is annotated only as 'Lsec: 20.0'; no numeric count values are legible, so peak intensities cannot be quantified

panel (d): the fine internal contrast within the red BCC matrix cannot be resolved at the supplied resolution, so δ-ferrite and ά-martensite cannot be separated visually although the caption lists both as BCC
panel (b): the exact boundaries between δ-ferrite and α/γ are marked by faint white lines only; individual lath dimensions are not readable
